module

public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Computability.BitstringEncoding
public import Mathlib.Computability.TuringMachine.Computable

/-!
# Complexity Classes

This file contains formal definitions of notions from complexity theory,
including the complexity classes P, NP, and coNP.

*References:*
- Sanjeev Arora and Boaz Barak. Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach.
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Computability Turing

namespace ComplexityTheory

/--
The type of decision problems.

We define these as functions from lists of booleans to booleans,
implicitly assuming the usual encodings.
-/
abbrev DecisionProblem := List Bool → Bool

/--
The type of complexity classes. We define these as sets of decision problems.
-/
abbrev ComplexityClass := Set DecisionProblem

/--
`IsPolyTimeWithEncoding ea eb f` asserts that `f` is computable in polynomial time
when its input and output are encoded via the given `Encoding`s `ea` and `eb`.
-/
def IsPolyTimeWithEncoding {α β Γα Γβ : Type} (ea : Encoding α Γα) (eb : Encoding β Γβ)
    (f : α → β) :=
  Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea.encode eb.encode f)

/--
A function is polynomial-time computable when it is `IsPolyTimeWithEncoding`
for the canonical `Bool`-alphabet encodings of its domain and codomain
as given by the `BitstringEncoding` typeclass.
-/
def IsPolyTime {α β : Type} [BitstringEncoding α] [BitstringEncoding β] (f : α → β) : Prop :=
  IsPolyTimeWithEncoding (BitstringEncoding.toEncoding (α := α)) (BitstringEncoding.toEncoding (α := β)) f

/-- The identity function is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem isPolyTime_id {α : Type} [BitstringEncoding α] : IsPolyTime (id : α → α) :=
  ⟨Turing.idComputableInPolyTime BitstringEncoding.bitEncode⟩

/- ## Class definitions -/

/--
The class P is the set of decision problems
decidable in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine.
-/
def P : ComplexityClass :=
  { L | IsPolyTime L }

/--
The class NP is the set of decision problems
such that there exists a polynomial `p` over ℕ and a poly-time Turing machine
where for all `x`, `L x = true` iff there exists a `w` of length at most `p (|x|)`
such that the Turing machine accepts the pair `(x,w)`.

See Definition 2.1 in Arora-Barak (2009).
-/
def NP : ComplexityClass :=
  { L | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ), ∃ R : (List Bool × List Bool) → Bool,
      IsPolyTime R ∧
      ∀ x, L x ↔ ∃ w : List Bool, w.length ≤ p.eval x.length ∧ R (x, w) }

/--
The class coNP is the set of decision problems
whose complements are in NP.
-/
def coNP : ComplexityClass :=
  { L | Lᶜ ∈ NP }

end ComplexityTheory

reformulations.difference: The canonical BitstringEncoding instance encodes each input bit b as [true, b, false], rather than presenting the original binary string directly to the machine.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This encoding and its inverse on valid encodings are linear-time transformations, with encoded length exactly 3 times the original length. A decider in either representation yields one in the other by encoding or decoding before running it; malformed encodings can be rejected in linear time. Mathlib's finite-control multi-stack machines and ordinary deterministic Turing machines also simulate each other with polynomial overhead. Thus this defines the usual class P. The exact encoding-length formula was proved in scratch.lean, but the complete machine-simulation equivalence was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: Arora–Barak Definition 2.1 uses certificates of exactly polynomial length. Lean uses length at most p.eval x.length, with p : Polynomial ℕ and a canonically encoded pair as verifier input.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An exact-length verifier becomes a bounded-length verifier by rejecting witnesses of the wrong length. Conversely, pad a bounded-length witness to the prescribed length and have the new verifier test every prefix of the padded string. There are only linearly many prefixes, so polynomial-time verification is preserved, including for empty witnesses. Natural-coefficient polynomials suffice by majorizing any polynomial bound and retaining any necessary original length check. The pair encoding has length 6|x| + 3|w| + 1, so it preserves polynomial bounds in the combined input length. padding.lean proves the witness-existence iff; the full equivalence including polynomial-time preservation was justified algorithmically, not proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The use site asks about the total function Nat.primeFactorsList on all naturals, returning a sorted list with multiplicities, whereas the source discusses factoring positive integers without fixing this output representation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Nat.primeFactorsList agrees with prime factorization for positive inputs, including the empty factorization of 1. Its value [] at 0 is a harmless finite extension: a polynomial-time positive-input algorithm can detect zero separately, and the converse follows by restriction. Sorting and converting a prime factorization to this list takes polynomial time: there are at most log₂(n) prime factors counted with multiplicity and polynomially many output bits. The natural-number input encoding is binary. IsPolyTime concerns existence of a machine computing the function, not the runtime of its particular Lean implementation.
